name: Mississippi
summary: Statutes: the only government route to the Mississippi Code is LexisNexis's free unannotated container (JavaScript, no text to either tool), and the Legislature's hosts fail TLS verification, so Justia's 2025 Code (tier 2, WebFetch only; built section URLs verified) is the text source. Constitution: SOS annotated PDF ('updated May, 2022'; script reads all 193 pp). Court rules: courts.ms.gov PDFs for M.R.C.P., M.R.E., M.R.A.P., MRCrP, Professional Conduct, UCRCCC and UCCR are script-readable (corpus candidates). Case law: date-constructible SCT/COA hand-down lists (observed 2000-2026) link opinion PDFs with ¶ numbering; the Court's docket search is robots-disallowed, so Justia (constructible from docket + decision year) is the docket finder. Cert grants/denials appear on Supreme Court hand-down lists under -CT-…-SCT dockets. Admin code: SOS app returns no text; Cornell LII per-rule pages are constructible.

citation_map.notes: No public-domain citation: Mississippi cites So. 3d (So. 2d / So. earlier; 'Miss.' official reports ended 1966) with ¶ pinpoints, e.g. '345 So. 3d 512, 516 (¶11) (Miss. 2022)'; slip opinions are identified by docket '{year}-{type}-{5 digits}-{SCT|COA}' (types include CA civil, KA criminal, CP civil pro se, KM, CT certiorari, IA interlocutory, DP death penalty direct appeal, DR death-penalty post-conviction, SA state agency, FC federal certified question, R rules). The -SCT/-COA suffix is distinctive, so docket numbers route here without context. A petition for certiorari from a Court of Appeals decision becomes '{year}-CT-{number}-SCT' (same number as the COA case — from memory; CT dockets observed on hand-down lists). Bare 'Section 15-1-49' (Mississippi's own style) is shared with Alabama and others: context_required. 'MRPC' is also used by Michigan and Minnesota: context_required; 'M.R.E.'/'MRE' are shared with Michigan: context_required; 'Miss. R. Prof'l Conduct' is distinctive. 'M.R.C.P.', 'M.R.E.', 'M.R.A.P.' are Mississippi's house abbreviations; Montana/Maine use 'M. R. Civ. P.'/'M.R. Civ. P.' which these regexes do not match (C must be followed by P). 'cert. denied' routes here only with Mississippi context. A '§§ 11-9-101 to -147' range takes the first section only. CourtListener ids miss / missctapp from memory, unverified. Constitution: Justia's page holds only §§ 1-183, so higher sections route to the SOS PDF first (already first in routes_to). 'URCCC N.NN' citations to pre-2017 criminal chapters (6-12) do not exist in the current UCRCCC PDF (Rules 1.01-5.10): send criminal-practice cites to the Rules of Criminal Procedure. The marked Code pattern accepts 'of the Miss. Code' as well as 'of the Mississippi Code'.

access.pattern_rules: Title and chapter from the citation (15-1-49 → title-15/chapter-1/section-15-1-49/). Chapters divided into articles add /article-{n}/; the article is not in the citation: read it from the chapter index, whose links show '§§' ranges (e.g. 'Article 3 - Justice Courts (§§ 11-9-101 - 11-9-147)'). Title indexes show chapter §§ ranges, or 'Arts. 1 - 3' for chapters with articles. Year editions: insert /{year}/ after /mississippi/.
access.navigation: title index (chapter links with §§ ranges; 'Arts.' marks a chapter with articles) → if 'Arts.', open the chapter index and pick the article by §§ range → section page.
